newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - June 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - June 20.

text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Indonesian press on June 20. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

The Moslem-based United Development Party (PPP) has refused to grant its excess votes to the fragmented Indonesian Development Party (PDI), which cannot meet the required minimum 11 seats in the House of Representatives due to its poor showing in general elections last month. The ruling Golkar party, which swept the May 29 general elections, has so far indicated it is willing to trade votes to help the PDI.
Importers have said the customs electronic data interchange (EDI) system is still beset with problems and only 222 or 2.7 percent of the 8,000 licensed importers have been connected to the system.
The World Bank has said the government should adopt a more transparent, market-oriented strategy to solve problems in the banking sector and take timely action to penalise chronic offenders.
Polyester manufacturer Indorama has said it will go ahead with a plan to invest $250 million in the industry despite sluggish business.
